name: The Sealed Core
summary: A plains faith holding that a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal: the material was never a resource but a sacrament, and the Iron Grief was the one generation that broke its own seal and lost the vein. It exists because a tier with no spatial law cannot open fresh rock, so the only answer to running out is a rule about why ore was owed at all.

attributes.what_it_explains: Why there is no more iron: the vein was sealed against an appetite, and a generation opened it to climb, and the seam has been shut ever since.
attributes.what_it_demands: One initiation, paid in worked ore from the temple's own face, and a socket cemented in the public forge with no hood over the furnace.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Opening a living body, reforging a socket, and heating a temple furnace with spirit stone bought from above the ridge.
attributes.who_holds_office: Only a Binder whose own socket was sealed in this temple; the caste is closed because a second seal is forbidden.
attributes.what_happens_to_a_dissenter: The forge record marks the person's socket void. No lawful Binder anywhere will then certify them, and in a tier where certification gates ascent the exclusion is a body that cannot finish forming.
attributes.temple_land: The Ore Under the Ash, worked by the temple rather than sold, which is the only ground on the plains whose output is consecrated instead of traded.
attributes.court: A bond court of Binders only, which will hear a contract between two households and will not hear a dispute about the seal itself.
attributes.marriage_law: Two sealed sockets may be bound; a marriage with one unsealed party is permitted and is entered as unfinished, which affects inheritance and nothing else.
attributes.feast_calendar: The Unsealed Night, once a year, when every socket in the temple's book is opened, sealed and re-cemented in public.

name: The Unsealed Assembly
summary: The plains' agnostic house: nothing was sealed, nothing survives, and there is no second frame for a person to arrive in. It exists because it is the only afterlife claim the six-group law budget actually permits, and because a body on the lowest tier is a fire spending itself whether or not anyone supervises the spending.

attributes.what_it_explains: Only what can be measured inside one frame, and it holds that a story about a second frame is a claim about somebody's standing rather than a claim about the universe.
attributes.what_it_demands: Refusal of titles, refusal of the gate-fee crowds, and publication of your own figures, including the ones that make you look foolish.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Any institution that certifies another body, any land held by a congregation, and any doctrine of what follows a death.
attributes.who_holds_office: Nobody. It runs one arbitration bench, drawn by lot, seated once and dissolved the same hour, and refuses to keep the office afterwards.
attributes.what_happens_to_a_dissenter: Nothing, and that is the cost it publishes: there is no membership to lose, so there is also nothing that will stand between an excluded person and whoever excluded them.
attributes.afterlife_claim: None. It holds the question malformed rather than unanswered, on the ground that a second frame would need a seventh law group and there are six.
attributes.membership_test: Produce a figure you did not want published. There is no other test and there is no fee.

name: The Gale Vigil
summary: The faith of the Sixfold Ridge: a border with no season in it cannot be given a timetable, so somebody must stand on it every hour of every year by rotation, and its god is the flock that arrives. It exists because a spirit-tier frame that left elemental law unwritten has no calendar, and it is openly hostile to Mind Dao, which teaches that the self can leave and nobody on that ridge ever has.

attributes.what_it_explains: Why the pass is opened on the flock's schedule and closed on nobody's, and why the holder of the crossing sets a price and never a date.
attributes.what_it_demands: One adult per household per rotation at the ridge, with no payment, no exemption and no record of who refused.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Any teaching that describes the self leaving the body, on the grounds that such a teaching is a recruiting promise made to people who cannot leave.
attributes.who_holds_office: Gale Keepers, conscripted by rotation rather than ordained; the office is held for one rotation and is surrendered afterwards without comment.
attributes.what_happens_to_a_dissenter: Turned off the pass. The ridge is the only way across, so the exclusion is carried out by the dissenter's own community.
attributes.what_it_demands_of_the_dead: The Return of the Flock is the only observance, and a body is buried above the last measured tide mark, because a body left below it is a body the flock will not find again next year.
attributes.host_to_dao: Mind Dao, for a reason that is economic before it is doctrinal: the only bodies that can leave are the ones with somewhere to go, and the ridge has exactly one exit.

name: The Ledger of Names
summary: The faith of the immortal court, holding that an office is a titled entity and an empty one is not a failure but a held breath. It exists because the Vacancy Decree made vacancy a state the setting can write down, and because a tier with ten seats, six laws and four unfillable slots has to have an answer for what an office is when there is nothing to seat in it.

attributes.what_it_explains: Why four seats in nine cannot be filled and why the seats above them are not filled either: a slot cannot hold what does not exist, and a named office is more than the person standing in it.
attributes.what_it_demands: One entry per office per period, including the vacant ones, written in the same hand and the same ink as the filled ones.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Appointing by decree, closing a register entry to save a page, and speaking about an unfilled seat in the future tense.
attributes.who_holds_office: Whoever passed a trial the naming office cannot judge. The faith adds nothing to that and takes nothing from it, which is the entire reason the Regency tolerates it at the centre of its own government.
attributes.what_happens_to_a_dissenter: Their objection is entered with the vacancy set beside it. The discipline is that no dispute outranks the register, so the worst a dissenter receives is a very long entry.
attributes.afterlife_claim: The Ninth Wait: a person is waited for by a seat, and the office outlives its officeholder, which is the only afterlife in the setting that hands power to the dead.
attributes.temple_land: None. The Church of Names holds no ground and no ore; its entire capital is the standing to certify that a seat is empty.
attributes.split: No One Lends the Seat left over the question of whether a vacancy may be blessed, and the split is why the court now keeps two registers.

name: The Last Measure
summary: The faith of the highest tier, holding that a law can be held apart from its effect and read, and that the reading is the only sacred act. It exists because fifteen seats over three layers is the only composition in the setting with real slack, and because an observation that must be repeated costs more lifetimes than that tier has.

attributes.what_it_explains: Why the highest tier is the only place anything can be measured instead of obeyed, and why almost nobody is ever shown a result.
attributes.what_it_demands: One observation, held by one body, with no assistance and no second attempt; the person who completes one may never begin another.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Predicting a result, repeating an observation on a schedule, and recruiting. A faith that could be taught at scale would be run at scale, and a tier that can staff its own practice stops being able to hold itself.
attributes.who_holds_office: The Floor Clerks, one per observation, dissolved when it ends, holding no seat in the court and no title afterwards.
attributes.what_happens_to_a_dissenter: Nothing, and the faith is proud of it: nothing here can be excommunicated because nothing here is a membership. The Unpaid Hours exist precisely because that pride is itself a practice somebody can keep.
attributes.afterlife_claim: Burial Below the Frame: a body is placed in the third layer, where fifteen imprints leave nine slots of surplus and somewhere to put it. The unreachable part is the point.
attributes.cost: The clerk's lifespan is a rounding error on a clock running ten to a hundred times a mortal's, so the office is a one-use body and the faith treats the body as the fee.

name: The Flat Liturgy
summary: The largest congregation on the plains and the Sealed Core's excommunicated majority: it keeps the ore rites and drops the theology, holding that a core is a cavity and a cinder is a process. It exists because the Core charges an initiation fee in worked ore, and a faith that shuts the rite to anyone without money has left the largest market on the tier unheld.

attributes.what_it_explains: That a core is a cavity and a cinder is heat, and that the ceremony works because ore holds qi, which is a property of the world rather than a promise about anything.
attributes.what_it_demands: Attendance at the cinder and nothing else: no fee, no socket, no register entry and no office of any kind.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Claiming a seat, binding a household, and calling the rite sacred. The third of those is the specific act that earned the excommunication.
attributes.what_happens_to_a_dissenter: Nothing, because there is nothing to be expelled from. Its refusal to certify anybody is exactly what the Sealed Core could not tolerate next door.
attributes.split_cause: The initiation fee. A third of the Sealed Core's congregations could not pay it and were told plainly that the rite was closed to them.
attributes.relationship_to_the_rite: It performs the Core's sealing with the priest's words left out, and the omission is the whole of its heresy, because the words are what make the operation a rite rather than a repair.

name: The Writ of Refusal
summary: A spirit-tier denomination forbidding any of the three Daos to be taught to a child before the child can read the law census itself, and it names Body Dao first, because Body Dao's home tier licenses no humanoid, so every teacher of it on the plains is a visitor collecting a gate fee. It exists because a doctrine delivered by a non-resident is a tariff, and a tier whose only export is an audience has no defence.

attributes.what_it_holds_of_all_three_daos: That none of them may be taught before the Law Census has been read by the student, and that a teaching given by somebody the frame itself classes as a visitor is a tariff rather than a truth.
attributes.who_it_targets: Body Dao first, on the economic argument. It holds that a doctrine whose only teachers live above the ridge and charge admission at the gate has stopped being a philosophy and become an import.
attributes.what_it_demands: A child who can name the six law groups and say which three the mortal frame actually seats, before any of the three readings is mentioned to them.
attributes.what_it_demands_of_dissenting_teachers: None. The Writ refuses to ban; it forbids only the order of instruction, and that difference is the entire dispute with the Sealed Core, which bans.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Charging for initiation, seating a child into a path before the census is read, and calling any Dao native to a tier it cannot reproduce itself in.
attributes.consequence: It is the only institution in the setting that publishes a reading list, and the only one the Quarrywright has never attempted to buy.

name: No One Lends the Seat
summary: A splinter of the Church of Names that will not perform a rite at all, holding that a vacant seat is a mechanical fact, since a slot cannot hold what does not exist, and that blessing one is a comfort sold to the anxious. It exists because the Ledger's benediction is a fee nobody can refuse once they have started attending, and a denomination that performs nothing has to be the one that says so out loud.

attributes.what_it_believes: That vacancy is arithmetic. The Refused Seating consumed a slot on an absence and nothing since has produced a seventh group for the four unfillable seats, so there is nothing for a rite to address.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Any spoken observance of a vacancy, including the Seat Quiet, on the ground that naming an absence aloud once a period is a practice of making people feel better about it.
attributes.who_holds_office: Nobody, and the sect says so in its own register: it keeps a list of offices and writes nothing under any of them, including under its own.
attributes.what_it_demands: That a question about a seat be answered arithmetically. It will not accept an answer that begins with intent.
attributes.what_happens_to_a_dissenter: Disqualified from holding any seat by the other register. That is the sectarian cost, and the sect's whole argument is that it is the only cost anybody pays for a wrong belief.
attributes.relationship_to_the_ledger: It reads the same three-state vocabulary the Court of the Star uses and refuses the theology attached to it, which is exactly why both registers are kept and neither is suppressed.

name: The Unpaid Hours
summary: A split from the Last Measure by a clerk who completed an observation and then declined to let the office dissolve. It holds that the hour's discipline has stopped being a way of reading a law and become a way of holding a frame open indefinitely, which is Mind Dao's own practice performed by a faith that forbids practice.

attributes.what_it_believes: That a completed observation is not a result but a position, and that a body holding one position against fifteen imprints is not measuring anything. It is refusing to be moved.
attributes.what_it_changed: It kept the discipline and dropped the dissolution. The office is now permanent, which is the one clause the parent faith forbids.
attributes.relationship_to_mind_dao: It has no doctrine and one method, and the method is the top-tier reading of spatial and temporal law performed without the metaphysics, so the sect is the setting's clearest case of a faith turning into a technique.
attributes.what_it_costs: A body held against fifteen imprints must be fed, and the sect is the only congregation on the top tier that carries a standing upkeep bill.
attributes.what_happens_to_a_dissenter: Expelled with the reading time entered against their name, which on a clock running ten to a hundred times a mortal's is a sentence already measured in centuries.
attributes.relationship_to_the_parent: The Last Measure does not acknowledge it. The difference between a faith and a sect in this setting is entirely in whether the dissolution clause is honoured.

name: The Counterweight
summary: A school rather than a congregation, holding that the six law groups are the whole of what there is, that the three Daos are three incompatible local readings of the same six, and that a person may hold one, change one and owe nothing to any of them. It exists because the Dao factions hold territory instead of running schools, which leaves nobody teaching the arithmetic the factions' own doctrine rests on.

attributes.central_claim: Six groups, finite and shared. Three readings, each local to a tier whose budget can afford it. And no reading has standing above the frame it was read in.
attributes.position_on_the_daos: All three are tools. Adopting one is a decision about which frame you are standing in, and it is revoked without notice, ceremony or apology.
attributes.why_it_is_a_school: It teaches the seat budget and the authored ranges, which is the only curriculum in the setting that predicts anything, and it refuses to admit anyone who wants a lineage.
attributes.what_it_forbids: A permanent conversion, a hereditary teacher, and any sentence of the form a Dao holds true everywhere.
attributes.office: One classroom, a sliding bench, and a rule that whoever teaches leaves the bench for a year, so the school has no incumbent and therefore no seat to fill.
attributes.institutional_cost: The three factions each hold ground and teach nothing, and the Visitor Offices license nobody, so the only party in the setting that can explain why anything works is one nobody has ever thought to tax.

name: The School of the Closed Frame
summary: A school of law-reading that treats the universe as a closed budget and every doctrine of a seventh group as an arithmetic error rather than a mystery. It exists because the Refused Seating was actually attempted, the slot it consumed can no longer be told from an empty one, and the setting therefore needs a body that can prove the impossibility instead of only remembering the failure.

attributes.central_claim: A universe is the closed budget of six groups that exists once and whole. A world holds a subset, never a seventh, and no quantity of will substitutes for a group that does not exist.
attributes.method: Seat the last missing law in a test frame, diff what the frame newly permits, and write down which result caused which. The school's finding is negative and it is the whole curriculum: a spare seat is not capacity for a new path.
attributes.what_it_refuses: It refuses to treat the Refused Seating as a tragedy. It treats it as a solved problem and refuses any memorial vocabulary for it, which is the sharpest disagreement it has with the Church of Names.
attributes.office: One room at the sixth-seat grounds, unseated, unendowed and open to anyone who can do the diff, including the Glasskin descendants, who are the only people alive who have watched a law change from inside a body.
attributes.what_it_demands: That a claim about a law be stated as a claim about a dial and a value with the layer named. Vague law-talk is refused admission.
attributes.conflict: It holds that vacancy is arithmetic while the Church of Names holds it sacred, and both readings are kept on file at the court for exactly that reason.

name: The Thing Under the Seam
summary: The Sealed Core's object of worship, which is not a being: it is the pressure in the worked-out vein, held sacred as an appetite that has to be fed or it feeds. It exists because a faith whose central rite seals a core needs something to seal against, and because a god with a face could be bargained with, whereas an appetite cannot.

attributes.what_it_is: The remaining pressure below the exhausted seam. It is not alive, it does not answer, and it is treated as the second party to every rite, because a rite with one participant is a demonstration.
attributes.how_it_is_worshipped: By sealing. The ceremony is addressed outward, to the pressure, and the cinder is the offering; the deity is what the offering is set against.
attributes.what_it_cannot_do: It cannot be asked for anything. Petition is forbidden, and a member who petitions is expelled before the Expulsion, on the reasoning that an answered appetite is a misunderstanding about what is down there.
attributes.image: None. There is no carving, no painted likeness and no name carved anywhere, and the temple's inner wall is left bare with the reason written on it in the congregation's own hand.
attributes.office_toward_it: The Binders stand in for it. A Binder's only function is to hold a line, and the deity is an appetite, so the line is the entire priesthood.
attributes.evidence_for_belief: The seam's measured fall is roughly four decades deep and has produced no further cavity in all that time, which the congregation reads as proof that what is below is still there and still pressing.

name: The Nineteenth Seat
summary: The Church of Names' titled entity: the first of the four immortal seats that can never be filled, treated as a permanent member of the court with a calendar and no holder. It exists because the tier runs realms nineteen to twenty-seven, so the seat has an ordinal and a name, and because the Vacancy Decree forces the court to speak the word in the open.

attributes.what_it_is: Seat nineteen of the immortal tier, unfillable because a slot cannot hold what does not exist, and addressed anyway. The court enters it at the head of every list of seats it keeps.
attributes.what_it_receives: The Seat Quiet: once a period its vacancy is named aloud in the district below, because a vacancy that is never spoken cannot be told apart from an absence.
attributes.what_it_does: Nothing, deliberately. The faith holds that a seat is a claim on the future and that giving it any power would be a promotion nobody was ever tried for.
attributes.how_it_is_offended: By filling it, by closing the register page, and by the other three being quietly dropped from a list copied in a later hand.
attributes.relationship_to_the_offices: The Regency may name it and may not take it, and this deity is the reason that rule reads as piety rather than as an oversight.
attributes.evidence: The four duplicate imprints in the second layer and a reading that no candidate has ever been able to supply are the only two facts the faith requires.

name: The Swift That Returns
summary: The Vigil's god: a flock, not a being, and it is kept as an itinerary rather than addressed. It exists because elemental law is unwritten on the Sixfold Ridge, so the pass has no season and therefore no calendar, and the only schedule the frame can supply is one an animal repeats.

attributes.what_it_is: The pass swift, and its arrival is the calendar. Nothing on this ridge seats an element, so nothing here anchors a year, and the flock's return is the only event that recurs on its own.
attributes.how_it_is_kept: By opening the pass when it comes and closing it when it has gone. No calendar in the setting is more authoritative, and the holder of the toll has never once set a date.
attributes.what_it_is_asked_for: Nothing. There is no prayer and no offering, because a bird on a schedule is not a person and pretending otherwise is the exact error this faith exists to avoid.
attributes.relationship_to_the_dead: The Return of the Flock is the only observance, and a body is buried above the last measured tide mark so that the ground can be found again in a year with no other marker.
attributes.what_it_proves: That a world holding five of six laws and deliberately leaving the sixth unwritten can still keep a calendar, provided it accepts one that arrives rather than one that is declared.
attributes.office_toward_it: The Keepers stand on the pass all year by rotation. The deity is a schedule, so the priesthood is a shift roster.

name: The Binders
summary: The Sealed Core's priesthood, closed because a second seal is forbidden: a Binder's own socket must have been sealed in the temple they serve, which can happen exactly once. It exists because the Reckoning Seat certifies a breakthrough by a body the mortal tier is not licensed to produce, and a certification nobody with standing will issue is not a verdict.

attributes.admission: One lifetime, one socket, one temple. There is no second attempt anywhere in the setting, which is what makes the caste hereditary in practice without any law requiring it.
attributes.what_they_certify: That a body is sound enough to attempt a gate, certified in the public forge with the person present. The Reckoning Seat cannot pay them and cannot replace them.
attributes.what_they_refuse: To certify an unsealed socket, which is the whole of their monopoly: an unsealed body cannot be certified and therefore cannot be tested at the Cairn Field at all.
attributes.what_they_spend: The temple's worked ore, every certification they perform, and their own bodies at a forge with no hood over it.
attributes.what_a_binder_leaves_with: Nothing but the caste. A Binder cannot hold a household bond, cannot own ground and cannot be buried by the temple; they are buried as inventory with the socket recovered, and their consent is not required.
attributes.cost_of_the_office: A Binder's hands fail first. The forge takes the fine work and certification is the fine work, so a Binder's usefulness is the earliest thing in the institution to go.

name: The Floor Clerks
summary: The Last Measure's entire clergy: one clerk per observation, seated for the observation, dissolved when it ends, and forbidden by rule from ever being appointed twice by the same person. It exists because the highest tier's clock runs ten to a hundred times a mortal's, so an observation that must be repeated costs more lifetimes than the tier possesses.

attributes.appointment: One observation. The rule that a person may not be seated twice is enforced by there being no mechanism at all to record who was seated, which the faith considers stricter than any register.
attributes.what_they_do: Hold a single act of attention against fifteen imprints until it ends. They do not interpret it and they are not permitted to write anything down while holding it.
attributes.what_they_cannot_do: Assist, observe, take a second clerk, or answer a question put during the hour. The No-Answer Oath is what makes an observation worth recording as one.
attributes.what_the_office_is_worth: Nothing after the dissolution. A former clerk holds no title, no seat and no standing, and the faith's argument is that this is the only credential in the setting that cannot be inherited or seized.
attributes.relationship_to_the_held_hour: The Observatory College tends the floor and keeps the room; the clerks hold the observation and the College keeps the floor. Neither may take the other's function, and that separation is the only check either office has.
attributes.failure: A clerk who cannot complete an observation is recorded only as incomplete. The tier has no instrument that distinguishes incomplete from unwilling, and the faith refuses to invent one.

name: The Gale Keepers
summary: The Vigil's priesthood, which is not ordained and cannot be: one adult per household per rotation on the ridge, unpaid, unrecorded and unexemptable. It exists because a pass with no season cannot be handed to a standing garrison, since the holder would be paying wages every hour of a year with no forecast, so the frame's answer was conscription by household.

attributes.how_they_are_made: Not chosen. Each household on the ridge owes one adult for one rotation, and a household that has already given cannot give again for two rotations.
attributes.what_they_do: Stand at the pass and hold the crossing open or shut on the flock's schedule. There is nothing to do at a crossing that has been held all year, and that is the job in full.
attributes.pay_and_privilege: None, and no exemptions. A household that bought its way out is recorded publicly by the ridge and the name stays up for a generation.
attributes.what_they_may_not_do: Hold religious office, judge a dispute, or refuse a traveller. The third is forbidden absolutely, because a gate with a keeper who may refuse is a toll and not a pass.
attributes.relationship_to_the_toll_holder: The keeper collects nothing. The holder of the crossing collects, and the keeper's existence is what makes that collection defensible, which is why the two institutions are permanently obliged to each other.
attributes.why_it_is_a_priesthood: Because the faith holds no thing at all. It holds a duty with a roster, and the roster is the entire institution.

name: Forbidden: The Second Seal
summary: The Sealed Core's central prohibition: no socket may be opened once sealed, and reforging one is the one act the temple's own forge is not permitted to perform. It exists because a second seal is how the Iron Grief happened, since a generation opened a living core to see whether a higher gate would fit and the vein has been shut ever since, so the prohibition is the whole of this faith's content.

attributes.the_prohibition: No reforging of a sealed socket, on a living body or a dead one, and none for inspection. The temple forge exists to seal and is deliberately built so that it cannot do the other thing.
attributes.why_it_is_enforceable: The Binders' certification is the enforcement. An unsealed body cannot be certified, so the prohibition is not a rule but a wall with no door, and nobody has ever found the door.
attributes.the_exception: None. The congregation was asked once for a body-under-glass exemption and its answer is recorded and still displayed in the temple, in the handwriting of the person who wrote it.
attributes.what_it_protects: Nothing the congregation can name. It protects the appearance of permanence, which is what a body paying for its own permanence every year actually requires.
attributes.what_breaks_it_in_practice: The Flat Liturgy, which performs the sealing with the priest's words left out, and which is why a theological omission turned out to be a material one.
attributes.cost_of_enforcement: The temple's forge is public and uncapped. Anyone may watch a sealing and nobody may watch an unsealing, because there is nobody left who can perform one.

name: Forbidden: Naming a Debt
summary: The Unsealed Assembly's prohibition: no debt owed by a named person may be written down, and the prohibition binds the Assembly's own members first. It exists because the Assembly's entire claim is that no ledger stands above a person, and because the counting houses on every road answer that claim with a register, so the only available weapon was made illegal by the hand that held it.

attributes.the_prohibition: Publishing a debt owed by a named person, orally or in writing. A debt may be forgiven aloud in the debtor's presence, and that is the only act the Assembly recognises as extinguishing one.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because a written claim is the mechanism by which a person becomes an asset, and the Assembly's claim is that nobody is anybody's asset. The prohibition is the belief stated as law so that it cannot be quietly abandoned.
attributes.what_it_costs: Everything. An assembly that forbids the ledger cannot cite a ledger in a dispute, cannot seize a debtor and cannot prove a contract was ever made, so the exclusion of a dissenter has no mechanism and the dissenter knows it.
attributes.scope: Members first, then anyone within earshot of a meeting. It is enforced by refusal to deal rather than by any penalty, and the refusal is total.
attributes.relationship_to_the_counting_houses: Formally incompatible in both directions. The Saltledger cannot write an Assembly member's obligation and the Assembly cannot use a Saltledger contract, and neither will say the other's name in an argument.
attributes.why_it_still_exists: Because the Unwritten Count and the Standing Weight both decline to publish a price, and this prohibition is the only one of the three positions that has never been in a position to publish anything at all.

name: Forbidden: The Seventh Seat
summary: The highest-tier taught prohibition: the ritual, procedure and refusal by which a practitioner is taught not to seat a seventh law in a vacant slot. It exists because the Refused Seating was actually attempted, the slot it consumed can no longer be told from an empty one, and a failure nobody can certify as clean is a failure the next person to read the same records will attempt.

attributes.the_prohibition: No attempt to seat a law group outside the universe's budget, in any layer and at any value. Not attempted, not rehearsed, not argued for in public.
attributes.how_it_is_taught: As a diff. The student is handed an empty slot and the six authored groups and asked to seat one; when they cannot, they are shown the Refused Seating's own record and asked why that slot reads the same as a slot never touched.
attributes.why_it_is_the_most_expensive_knowledge_i: Because the attempt is the only way to be certain, because the failure cannot afterwards be certified clean, and because a world's tier is the only thing in the setting that can pay a bill like this. There is no cheaper proof and there is no second chance.
attributes.the_exception: The School of the Closed Frame runs the exercise in a test frame. That is the entire permission, and it exists because a prohibition nobody is permitted to test is a superstition rather than a proof.
attributes.what_the_dao_factions_do: None of the three teaches it. Each considers the question outside its reading, and the three together cover the whole legal space in which an attempt could be framed.
attributes.penalty: None. It is taught at the point where the student already knows the answer, because the faith's position is that a prohibition enforced by punishment has already failed and only the arithmetic holds.

name: Forbidden: The Exit
summary: The Vigil's prohibition on any teaching, text, story or practice that describes the self leaving the body, on the ground that such a teaching is a promise made to people with one road. It exists because Mind Dao is allied with Qi Dao and both operate a tier above the ridge, and because a garrison that has been told it can leave is a garrison that leaves.

attributes.the_prohibition: No account of the self leaving a body, including as metaphor, parable, allegory or genealogy. The Vigil's festival is a bird arriving and it is not read as anything else.
attributes.why_it_is_enforceable: The ridge hears everything. A duty roster of one adult per household is a distributed readership, so there is no room in which an account can circulate unreported.
attributes.the_argument: Not that the account is false. The Vigil's official position is that it is untested, expensive, and that its main effect is to recruit people out of a rotation they have already owed.
attributes.who_may_exempt: Nobody on the ridge. A traveller who teaches it is turned off the pass, and the exclusion is performed by the traveller's own household rather than by the faith.
attributes.what_it_costs_the_faith: It makes the Vigil the only institution in the setting openly at war with an allied pair of Daos, and it accepts that as the price of a roster it can actually staff.
attributes.relationship_to_the_counterweight: The school teaches all three Daos as adoptable tools and is refused entry to the ridge, which the school records as a result rather than as an injustice.

name: The Sealing of the Socket
summary: The Sealed Core's initiation: worked ore is brought from the temple's own face, the initiate's socket is opened and cemented in the public forge, and the amount used is entered in the register. It exists because the mortuary cycle and the initiation are the same operation, since a body is caged in ore at the start and returned to it at the end, and a faith separating them would be two institutions pretending to be one.

attributes.what_is_performed: A core-socket opened, cleaned, cemented with ore from the temple's own face, and entered in the register, with the whole congregation present.
attributes.what_it_costs: The initiate's fee in worked ore plus the temple's face, which is why the temple's output goes to cement and never to trade and why its land is held for the rite rather than for profit.
attributes.what_it_proves: Only that a seal holds today. The Unsealed Night exists precisely because a seal that is never opened cannot be known to hold at all, and the rite's own doctrine concedes this.
attributes.connection_to_the_dead: Identical in material and different in words: the same forge, the same ore, the same column of the register, with the single difference that nobody is watching for a result at a burial.
attributes.who_may_perform: A Binder, in the public forge, with the furnace unhooded. There is no private performance of this rite anywhere in the setting.
attributes.cost_of_refusal: The Flat Liturgy performs the same cement without the words, which is legal under the Second Seal prohibition and heresy under everything else, and the congregation has never formally answered which it thinks that is.

name: The Hour of the Floor
summary: The Last Measure's rite: one clerk holds one act of attention against the floor of the third layer until it ends, and nobody is permitted to organise the next one. It exists because a law can only be read where there is a surplus to hold it apart from its effect, and because the rite is designed so that no congregation accumulates: the next hour has no administrator, which is the whole institution.

attributes.what_is_performed: One clerk, one act of attention, held until it ends. No second participant, no instrument, no preparation and no recording while it is held.
attributes.duration: Unknown in advance and never announced. The room's rate of ascent to the floor is the only reason a clerk's lifespan is short, and the faith declines to treat that as a cost worth naming.
attributes.what_it_produces: A reading and nothing else. It is not interpreted, not published, and the clerk may speak of it for the rest of their life only to say that they completed it.
attributes.who_may_perform: One person. The No-Answer Oath makes an answer during the hour a breach, and that is what stops a half-completed hour being reported afterwards as a result.
attributes.the_unorganisable_clause: The rite cannot be scheduled and cannot be inherited. No mechanism exists to record a clerk, and the Unpaid Hours arose precisely because one clerk found a way to sit down twice.
attributes.standing_observers: The Held Hour tends the floor and keeps the room. They may not observe, and the clerks may not tend, because a floor-tender who watches is a second clerk by another name.

name: The Return of the Flock
summary: The Vigil's only observance and the setting's only festival whose date nobody chooses: the pass is opened when the flock comes and closed when it has gone. It exists because a frame with elemental law unwritten has no season, and because a garrison conscripted by rotation needs one shared date more than it needs a doctrine.

attributes.what_is_performed: The crossing is opened for the length of the flock's passage and closed after it. Every Keeper rotation is scheduled against it, so the roster and the rite are the same document.
attributes.when_it_happens: When the birds come. Nobody declares it and nobody can be late for it, which is the only scheduling guarantee available in a frame with no elemental seat to anchor a year.
attributes.what_is_forbidden_during_it: Closing the pass early, closing it late, and holding any other rite on the ridge, because a conscripted congregation cannot be asked to attend two things.
attributes.what_it_cost_the_polity: Galehold sets the toll and never the date, and this is the single reason that arrangement is defensible: the one calendar nobody can buy is the one calendar everybody obeys.
attributes.the_burial_conjunction: A body is buried above the last measured tide mark on the same principle, so that in a year with no other marker at all the ground itself remains findable.
attributes.attendance: Everyone on the ridge who can walk, plus every traveller standing on it at the time. It is the only occasion in the setting at which a stranger is counted as present.

name: Burial as Inventory
summary: The Sealed Core's burial law: the dead are opened, their usable ore recovered to the forge, and the register records how much. It exists because the plains' only dense material is the ore a core can be caged in, and because a faith that seals a body at initiation cannot then leave the material unreturned without admitting its own rite was theatre.

attributes.what_is_done: The body is opened within the day, the socket's contents are recovered to the temple forge, and the amount is entered in the register against the person's name.
attributes.what_the_family_keeps: Nothing physical. The register entry, the socket's own seal, and the assurance from the Unsealed Court that the core has resumed work are what the household is given.
attributes.why_no_graves: Because ground here cannot be returned to. A three-slot world seats no spatial law, so the heap at the Exhausted Seam has stood for four decades and a grave is simply one more thing that stays.
attributes.the_intimate_cost: Every burial is performed by people the household sees daily, and the congregation's etiquette is that this is discussed as labour and never as grief, which is not cruelty but a shared refusal.
attributes.what_the_register_becomes: A second census. The Church of Names' own clerks read it, and those two registers are the reason a body's material history survives long after its name has been culled from every household record.
attributes.who_may_claim_a_body: The congregation that sealed it, and nobody else, which is the entire material content of what excommunication from the Sealed Core actually means.

name: The Unkept
summary: The Unsealed Assembly's death rite: no preparation, no site, no marker, and one line in a hand that is immediately destroyed, because the body was ours and now it is not. It exists because the Assembly forbids a ledger and a grave is a ledger impossible to delete, and because a body left unmarked on ground that does not disperse is the only honest ending its doctrine admits.

attributes.what_is_done: The body is carried out by whoever was nearest and returned to whatever the ground will take. There is no preparation, no washing, no waiting period and no fixed hour.
attributes.what_is_written: Nothing durable. One line naming the person as ours is spoken aloud once and not written down, because the Assembly's prohibition on named records does not stop at death.
attributes.what_is_forbidden: A marker, a stone, a named plot, a standing stone and any year-on-year returning. A grave is treated as a claim and a returning is treated as a debt.
attributes.consequence_on_the_plains: The dead are unrecoverable, which is the serious operational argument against the practice, and the Assembly's answer is that a recovery carried out by a person is a person who must keep answering for it.
attributes.the_carrionfolk_collision: On ground where carrionfolk work an unmarked body is consumed within a day, and the Assembly treats this as the rite completing itself rather than as a failure of the rite.
attributes.the_dissenter_clause: A person excluded while alive is buried by the community that excluded them, because the Assembly cannot hold a grave and will not pretend otherwise. Exclusion therefore costs the excluder a body.

name: The Empty Chair
summary: The Church of Names' rite for an office rather than for a person: the chair is emptied, the entry stays open, and the calendar continues uninterrupted. It exists because an office outlives its holder by construction, since every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, and because a rite that ended the calendar would turn every death at court into a stoppage.

attributes.what_is_done: The chair is emptied, the register entry is left open with no name in it, and the next period's obligations are entered as though the seat were filled.
attributes.who_is_mourned: The person, by their household, in whatever way their household does it. The Church of Names has no rite for a person at all and holds that the distinction is the whole content of its theology.
attributes.the_clause_that_matters: The calendar is never interrupted. A death at court does not suspend an audit, a trial or a reading, which is the reason the court has never once needed to appoint anybody by decree in order to keep moving.
attributes.what_happens_to_the_chair_itself: It is not destroyed, not moved and not stored. It stays in the district below where it can be seen, because an office that cannot be seen empty is indistinguishable from an office that does not exist.
attributes.the_exception: A seat that can never be filled is not emptied, because it was never occupied, and the Nineteenth Seat is named at the Seat Quiet rather than mourned.
attributes.consequence: The Church of Names cannot be abolished by anybody, since the only thing it does is continue, and continuation has no single moment that can be interrupted.

name: The Grave of the Unnamed
summary: The cost of exclusion made explicit: a body excluded from a congregation is buried by the congregation that excluded them, and the law requiring it is written down in the excluded party's own name. It exists because an institution that will not hold a grave cannot exclude anybody without handing the body to somebody, and a law that makes the excluder pay is the only enforcement a body with no property can afford.

attributes.the_rule: Whoever excludes a person from a congregation that buries its own dead accepts the duty of burying them, in their name, in writing, at the exclusion's own expense.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because the Assembly's prohibition on holding a grave means it cannot shelter anybody, and a faith with no shelter should say so plainly rather than discover it at somebody's death.
attributes.who_enforces_it: Nobody. The Assembly has no office and the law has no court, so enforcement is the plain fact that the excluded person's neighbours have heard the name read aloud and now pay attention.
attributes.what_the_name_does: It becomes the only durable record of the exclusion. On the plains a name can be culled from every household ledger, and this is the one entry that survives because its author did not benefit from writing it.
attributes.cost_in_practice: Small on the plains, where there is no ground that holds anything, and large in spirit-tier settlements, where a grave is a plot, a wall and a location anybody may be shown.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Burying an excluded person as an unattributed loss. The rite requires a named grave, which is all of its teeth and the only written record the Assembly will ever produce.
attributes.relationship_to_the_empty_chair: The two are opposites and together they cover every way a person can end up without a place: the Church of Names holds a seat open and the Assembly holds nothing at all.

name: Burial Below the Frame
summary: The Last Measure's burial law: bodies are placed in the third layer, where fifteen imprints leave nine slots of surplus and somewhere for anything to go. It exists because the highest tier is the only composition in the setting with real slack, and because a body above ground on the surface layer stands in the way of an observation.

attributes.the_rule: Every body goes down. The surface layer is reserved for the standing and the held, and a body at the surface is an obstruction the clerks must work around.
attributes.why_there_is_room: Nine of the fifteen imprints at the highest tier are surplus duplicates spread over three layers, so the third layer holds the only genuine spare volume anywhere in the setting.
attributes.the_cost: No recovery. Nothing placed in the third layer comes back up, and the faith treats that as the price rather than as a defect, on the reasoning that a recoverable corpse would be a body somebody might want.
attributes.what_it_replaces: A funeral. There is no service, no procession and no assembly, because there is nothing to attend to and the third layer is not a place a mourner can stand.
attributes.relationship_to_the_hour: Every burial makes an observation marginally easier, which the faith records without comment and which is the closest thing it has to a doctrine of merit.
attributes.who_decides: The Floor Clerks, as the only people who know what the third layer is currently doing. This is the sole authority the Last Measure recognises anywhere in the setting.

name: No Residue
summary: The Unsealed Assembly's afterlife, stated as a malformed question rather than an answer: there is no second frame to arrive in, because a second frame would need a seventh law group and there are six. It exists because it is the only afterlife claim the law budget actually permits, and because every rival afterlife is a claim somebody is being paid to keep repeating.

attributes.the_claim: Not annihilation and not continuation. The question has no referent, because a self that ends has nothing to continue into and continuing needs somewhere to continue in.
attributes.the_argument: The universe is the closed budget of six groups and every world holds a subset. A place to arrive in would be another frame, and a frame carrying a seventh group is the exact thing the Refused Seating failed to make.
attributes.what_it_implies_for_grief: Nothing at all. The Assembly's cruelty is that it offers no consolation of any kind, and a mourner is told what was true and is not told it was meant to be otherwise.
attributes.what_its_rivals_say: That it is cowardice, and that a people who expect nothing have arranged never to be disappointed. The Assembly publishes this objection in full, which is the only thing about it its enemies respect.
attributes.who_is_buried_by_it: Nobody. The Unkept does not hold a body, so this belief is never tested by a death, which is the sharpest criticism of it and also the reason it has never been refuted.
attributes.relationship_to_the_unsealed_court: Direct opposition and not merely doctrinal. The Court holds that dead cores resume work, and if that is true then a measurable amount of it is happening in the frame right now.

name: The Unsealed Court
summary: The Sealed Core's afterlife: the dead are unsealed at burial and their core resumes work in the frame, so a body is fuel and the dead are fuel not yet spent. It exists because it is the load-bearing myth of an ore economy, being the reason ore is a sacrament rather than a commodity, and because a congregation recovering material from the dead needs them to still be doing something with it.

attributes.the_claim: Death ends the person and not the core. The core is unsealed by the burial rite and resumes work in the frame, which is why burial is a supply operation rather than an abandonment.
attributes.why_it_is_needed: Because the ore recovered is the ore the dead were caged in, and a faith that returned it while claiming the person had survived would be caught out at the first audit. This belief resolves that by making the residue the point.
attributes.the_carrionfolk_problem: Carrionfolk metabolise qi out of the dead and store none. On their ground the Unsealed Court and ordinary scavenging are indistinguishable, which the temple records as a local variant and elsewhere as a question it declines to answer.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Claiming that the dead are present. Resumption is not company, and a mourner who speaks to the core is corrected by their household rather than comforted.
attributes.the_cost_of_believing: A living person is a partly spent asset, which is why this faith's ethics are about maintenance rather than morality and why nobody in it has ever been comforted by it.
attributes.relationship_to_the_ninth_wait: The rival that keeps power with the dead. One says the dead work, the other says the office survives, neither has converted the other, and both registers are kept at the court for exactly that reason.

name: The Ninth Wait
summary: The Church of Names' afterlife: a person is not judged but waited for, and the thing that outlives them is the office they left. It exists because a tier with nine realms and four unfillable seats has produced an authority built entirely out of vacancies, and because that authority needs the dead to keep standing in its ledger.

attributes.the_claim: A person is not judged and does not go anywhere. What continues is the office, and it waits, which is why a dead officeholder is entered in the register as pending rather than as finished.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because the Empty Chair rite has to continue the calendar, and a doctrine in which the office is the durable thing is the only one that makes that rite honest rather than merely convenient.
attributes.what_the_dead_own: Their unperformed obligations, indefinitely. On a clock running five to fifty times a mortal's the debt is settled by successors, and the register keeps the original name standing against it.
attributes.what_it_forbids: A funeral that closes the entry. The record is not finished by a death, and the household's mourning is recorded separately and never merged into the seat's line.
attributes.the_danger: An office that is waited for is an office nobody can be released from, which is how the court produces heirs who do not want the post and cannot decline it visibly.
attributes.relationship_to_the_unsealed_court: Both keep the dead present in an institutional way and neither is accepted by the other, and the court permits both registers for the same reason it also permits the school's refutation.

name: The Opening Payment
summary: The Sealed Core's creation myth, and it is correct: somebody had to pay to open a world at all and the bill was written in law seats, so every world is a receipt for the same payment and the six groups are a fixed supply the tiers compete over. It exists because a myth that reads the seat budget as money has already worked out why the fourth seat was never affordable.

attributes.the_myth: Nobody made anything. A world is opened by paying for it out of a fixed supply of six groups, whoever paid could afford three seats, and every tier since is a receipt for that same payment.
attributes.why_it_is_true: It agrees with the arithmetic the School of the Closed Frame works in. A universe is six groups that exist once and whole, a world holds a subset, the supply never grows and no world is ever free.
attributes.what_it_makes_sacred: The seat budget, and therefore the Refused Seating becomes a sin rather than a mistake, because a slot spent on an absence is money spent on nothing, which is the one transaction the myth cannot forgive.
attributes.what_it_forbids: A progenitor. There is no first figure in it and no intention in it, because a story with an author is a story about somebody's standing.
attributes.what_it_answers_nothing: Where the six came from, what is not a group, and why anything should exist at all. It is a fiscal myth and it is silent on all three, which the congregation considers honest.
attributes.feast_use: The first-breath observance takes a tithe from every socket on the year first opened, counted in ore, which is the myth performed as a collection.
attributes.relationship_to_the_hollow_first: The direct opposite. Both are creation myths; one says a world was paid for and one says there was no first anything. A temple on the plains holds one and a house on the ridge holds the other and neither has ever won.

name: The Hollow First
summary: The Unsealed Assembly's creation myth, which is not a myth at all: there was never a first anything, and a story that begins is an accounting fiction with a hidden payee. It exists because a congregation that forbids a ledger and a creator cannot produce a genesis, and because a belief with no progenitor cannot produce a funeral that means anything either.

attributes.the_myth: There is no first event. Any account that opens with one is a list of items that has been given a first line for the convenience of reading.
attributes.why_it_is_a_creation_myth_anyway: It occupies the slot, refuses the contents, and is performed at the same hour the Sealed Core performs its tithe. The Assembly keeps a festival in order to decline to say anything at all.
attributes.what_it_forbids: A progenitor, an intention, and any sentence of the form something began. Its published objection is that such a sentence always implies somebody who was owed.
attributes.what_it_lacks_as_a_result: Everything explanatory. It says nothing whatever about where the six groups came from, and its congregation holds that this is the correct quantity of knowledge for that question.
attributes.what_it_gives_the_congregation: No obligation to any prior generation, no ancestor owed and therefore no inheritable debt, which on a tier where line-narrowing is an active political programme is the entire point.
attributes.relationship_to_the_unowned_genealogy: The Voidborn line, with no origin and no admitting household, is the one case in the setting where this myth and the documented facts agree, and the Assembly declines to claim it as evidence either way.
attributes.relationship_to_the_opening_payment: Its opposite and its sworn enemy. Both are performed on the same night, deliberately, one hour apart, so that nobody can attend without hearing the other.

name: The Quiet Bell
summary: A heresy holding that the Glasskin were not killed when physical law was retuned but transferred, since a law does not create or destroy what it inscribes and only stops holding it, so a retune is a resurrection nobody is entitled to. It exists because the mechanism is true and because a belief that makes every death reversible destroys the one institution that keeps the dead.

attributes.the_claim: The Glasskin vitrified when a world's physical law was raised to make material harder and every existing body failed at once. This holds that a law does not kill what it inscribes, it stops holding it, and that the difference is recoverable by writing the law again.
attributes.why_it_is_dangerous: Because it is mechanically defensible. A law imprint is a group held at a value in a layer, so a body the law failed to hold is simply not the same thing as a body the law destroyed.
attributes.why_it_is_condemned: By the Church of Names, which keeps the register, and by the Field Registry, which keeps the burnt list. A doctrine making death reversible makes every entry in either book a provisional claim and therefore worthless as a record.
attributes.what_it_would_require_in_practice: Somebody to write the law back at its old value on a world that has already moved, at an upkeep nobody can settle. That is why the heresy has no recorded attempt and rather more than two thousand converts.
attributes.who_it_persuades: Precisely the people the other records have lost: the Glasskin's descendants, the culled branches, and anyone whose name was struck from a ledger. The appeal is entirely to the bereaved and never to the living.
attributes.status_note: Declared an error by two institutions that share no deity, no temple and no single interest. It is the setting's clearest case of an agreed condemnation without agreement on anything else.
attributes.relationship_to_the_closed_frame_school: The school teaches the diff that makes this heresy visible, does not endorse it, and is asked about it perhaps once a decade.

name: Form Without Charge
summary: A heresy of Form-Only Dao that does not merely drop the qi component but worships the absence: a form that cannot be spent cannot be lost, so a practice with no resource behind it is the highest state and anyone paying upkeep is the weaker one. It exists because a mortal-tier world spends its qi at the floor, which pushes every practitioner independently toward the same conclusion, and because a heresy nobody can test at a high realm cannot be refuted.

attributes.the_claim: Form persists without charge. Refine until nothing is left to be destroyed, treat every expenditure of qi as an avoidable loss, and hold that a body which never spends is a body which cannot be taken.
attributes.descent: It descends from Form-Only Dao, which is Body Dao's form-permanence claim with the qi component removed. This goes further and makes the removal the virtue rather than the loss.
attributes.why_it_is_reproducible: A three-slot world spends its qi slot at the floor of its range, so a practitioner who cannot draw qi anyway arrives here independently of any teacher, which is what makes it a mass position rather than a sect.
attributes.why_it_is_unrefuted: No court above the mortal band has tested it against a realm-nineteen body and at a floor qi there is no difference to observe. Its ceiling is the world's floor and not its adherents' skill.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Uptake. Any purchase of qi-dense material is treated as a concession, and the congregation keeps no temple, because a temple needs maintaining and maintenance is a cost.
attributes.the_doctrinal_awkwardness: It is hostile to all three Daos without naming any of them. Body Dao keeps the qi component, Qi Dao is built on spending it, and Mind Dao's leaving costs expenditure of a different kind entirely.
attributes.relationship_to_the_sealed_core: Mutually repellent and mutually silent. Both are body-path certainties about permanence on the same ground, and neither congregation has ever explained itself to the other.

name: The Ore Under the Ash
summary: The Sealed Core's material basis: the only worked ground on the plains held by an institution that does not sell its output, because the temple forge is public and its ore goes to cement and never to trade. It exists because a faith charging an initiation fee in ore must hold ore, and because otherwise the Quarrywright would be the only body on the tier holding dense material at all.

attributes.what_it_holds: One worked face with its own forge, held by the temple for the rite and not for the market, and the only ground on the tier whose output is consecrated rather than sold.
attributes.why_it_is_not_sold: Because the ore becomes cement and cement is the fee. Selling ore and buying it back for a rite would price the sacrality out of the single transaction the faith actually cares about.
attributes.who_works_it: The congregation, in rotation, including the Binders. It is the only large labour on the plains no counting house can rent out, which is the estate's real protection.
attributes.why_it_is_defensible: Because four decades of spoil stand uncarried on the seam floor and spatial law is unspent here, so the only workable ground on the tier is ground whose heap has already been moved by hand. The temple's position is a heap it has already paid for.
attributes.what_it_taxes: Nothing. The Exclusivity Petition on graded cloth was filed against a house that publishes technique, attendance and a chamber in exchange for discretion, and this estate publishes none of those; it publishes a register of sockets and nothing else.
attributes.vulnerability: A forge is a furnace and the estate has the same fuel question the Quarrywright has. If spirit stone ever reached the plains, the argument for public and unsold ore would end inside a season.

name: The Pass Sheds
summary: The Vigil's material basis: sheds on the Sixfold Ridge paid for in labour rotation and never in coin, which is why a faith with no doctrine can hold a border no garrison will staff. It exists because a holder of a toll needs somewhere to stand in the worst hours of the year, and because a frame with no season cannot forecast the staffing at all.

attributes.what_it_holds: Four sheds and one standing platform at the pass, built and maintained by the households that owe the rotation, in stone cut on the ridge itself.
attributes.how_it_is_paid_for: In labour, per rotation, never in coin. This is the whole of the Vigil's solvency: it has no treasury because it never pays a wage.
attributes.why_it_is_needed: Because the flock occupies the worst hours and elemental law is unwritten here, so there is no forecast to staff against. A shed standing empty for a month is cheaper than a garrison paid for a month nobody can predict.
attributes.who_owns_it: Nobody in the ordinary sense. The sheds belong to the rotation, and a household leaving the ridge leaves its labour in the walls, which is the closest approach to ownership the ridge has.
attributes.the_toll_arrangement: Galehold collects the toll and maintains the crossing; the sheds keep warm the people who hold it. Neither owns the other's function and each is indispensable, which is the whole stability of the arrangement.
attributes.what_it_cannot_do: Store anything. There is no warehouse on the pass, so a rotation's provisions must be carried in by hand, and that cost is what keeps the rotation honest.

name: The Empty List
summary: The Church of Names' entire capital: it holds no ground, no ore and no building, and owns one register of vacancies whose standing to certify that a seat is empty is a thing the Vacancy Decree made valuable. It exists because a decree that makes vacancy a state hands the power of naming it to somebody, and an institution owning only a name can be abolished by nobody.

attributes.what_it_holds: One register. No land, no buildings, no ore, no granary and no treasury, and it has survived four attempts to buy it by naming the holder alone.
attributes.why_a_list_is_property: Because the Vacancy Decree requires every office to be entered whether or not it is filled, and the Church of Names is the body whose entry nobody contests. Controlling the entry is controlling that seat's status in every other list.
attributes.how_it_is_protected: By having nothing to seize. No material asset means no raid is worth mounting and no confession can be extracted, which is the Unwritten Count's argument arriving a century later in clerical dress.
attributes.what_it_spends: Clerks, ink, and the Seat Quiet, one period a year in which every vacant seat is named aloud in the district below, which is a large expense in a district where saying the word is expensive.
attributes.what_it_is_worth: Access and never power. It may enter a name and may not appoint one, and that distinction is the only reason the court permits this estate to sit at the centre of its own government.
attributes.vulnerability: The School of the Closed Frame holds that vacancy is arithmetic rather than sacred, and if that reading ever became the court's official one this register would have nothing left to be worth.

name: The Unsealed Night
summary: One night a year on the plains when every socket in the temple's book is opened, sealed and re-cemented in public, and the congregation attends to check the entries against the register. It exists because a seal that is never opened cannot be known to hold, and because a faith forbidding the second seal has to answer the question its own prohibition creates.

attributes.when: Once a year, on a date the temple sets and the congregation is told four months in advance. It is the only fixed calendar date the plains hold, and it is therefore purely an agreement.
attributes.what_happens: Every sealed socket in the temple's book is opened, inspected, re-cemented and re-entered in front of the congregation, and the forge runs all night with nobody hooded.
attributes.the_problem_it_creates: Opening a sealed socket is the Second Seal. The observance is legal only because each socket is re-sealed in the same sitting, and the temple's argument is that a thing inspected and closed again has not been unsealed. No other congregation accepts this.
attributes.what_the_congregation_checks: The register against the person. Any member may ask to see any entry, and this is the only mechanism by which a wrong certification on the plains can ever be discovered.
attributes.who_pays: The estate's own ore, out of the same face. The night's draw is the largest single consumption of the year and it is why the deposit's rate of fall is a matter of public record.
attributes.attendance: Voluntary and effectively universal. The Flat Liturgy attends and does not seal, standing at the back, which is the closest the two congregations have come to anything.

name: The Seat Quiet
summary: One period a year in which every vacant seat in the immortal tier is named aloud in the district below, in register order, with no commentary. It exists because a vacancy nobody says out loud is indistinguishable from an absence, which is precisely the failure the Refused Seating left behind, where a consumed slot and an untouched one read the same.

attributes.when: Once a period, at a time announced and not chosen. The interval is fixed by the register's own period, which belongs to the court, so even this observance runs on somebody else's clock.
attributes.what_is_done: Every vacant seat is read aloud in register order by a clerk with no commentary and no petition from the floor. The four unfillable seats are named last, which is a formality.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because the failure this setting actually suffered is a slot that cannot be told from an empty one. Saying the word aloud once a period is the only available control on a defect no instrument in the setting can measure.
attributes.who_may_speak: The clerk. A voice from the floor asking whether a seat might be filled is answered by continuing the reading, because the observance has no procedure for stopping.
attributes.what_it_costs: Enormously and on purpose. Naming vacancies in a district where a vacancy invites a petition is the most politically expensive sentence anyone at that court can say, and the Church of Names says it once a period deliberately.
attributes.who_forbids_it: The No One Lends the Seat splinter, which holds that the reading is a comfort sold to the anxious. The Church of Names answers that comfort is not the objection and does not alter the practice.

name: The Two-Seal Oath
summary: Sworn once in a lifetime by every Binder: the second seal is the seal against the second seal, sworn with the temple's own forge open and written into the register before it is spoken. It exists because a prohibition has to be held by somebody with the power to break it, and because the only body in the setting trusted to perform a binding at all is the body that has bound itself hardest.

attributes.what_is_sworn: That if a sealed socket is ever opened for any reason the Binder will report it publicly before it is re-cemented, whoever performed the opening and including themselves.
attributes.how_it_is_sworn: Once, in the public forge, entered in the register before a word is spoken, and never again, because a second oath is not permitted and does not need to be.
attributes.what_it_binds: Not belief. The Binder need not hold the Core's theology at all, because the oath is enforced by the forge's record and by the caste's certification monopoly, so it holds on an unbeliever equally.
attributes.the_awkwardness: It forbids the act it also forbids everyone else from performing. A Binder is the only person authorised to seal and the only person who has sworn never to unseal, which is the whole design and the reason one caste holds both halves.
attributes.what_it_costs_the_swearer: Their hands, their own burial as inventory with the socket recovered, and their household's exclusion from every bond the temple's court hears. A Binder marries into a category of their own.
attributes.what_breaks_it: Nothing has. The register carries no second-seal entry in four decades, which the temple publishes annually as its principal evidence that its doctrine is more than a superstition.

name: The No-Answer Oath
summary: Sworn by every clerk before the Hour of the Floor: the observer may not answer a question asked during the hour, may not indicate a result and may not be relieved. It exists because a result reported before an observation ends is a guess about a law, and a guess about a law is a law nobody seated and therefore something the tier cannot account for.

attributes.what_is_sworn: That during the hour the clerk will not answer, will not signal, will not nod, and will not accept relief, including relief they asked for themselves before the hour began.
attributes.why_it_exists: Because the tier's entire resource is a law held apart from its effect, and any report made during the holding is a value nobody seated. A guess about a dial is a law the Court of the Star never voted on.
attributes.what_it_forbids_outside_the_hour: Nothing at all, and the contrast is deliberate. A clerk is silent for the duration and completely ordinary otherwise, which is what makes the silence legible as a duty rather than as an injury.
attributes.the_relief_clause: The only part with teeth. A clerk who breaks may not hold again, and on a clock running ten to a hundred times a mortal's that phrase means what it says without anybody needing to define a penalty.
attributes.what_it_costs: The clerk cannot be asked whether the hour went well by anyone who cares about them, for the rest of their life, and there is no exception available for the person asking.
attributes.why_it_is_load_bearing: Because the Hour of the Floor produces nothing observable, and this oath is the entire reason a silence can later be reported as an observation rather than as an absence.
attributes.relationship_to_the_unpaid_hours: The splinter exists because a clerk honoured this oath once and then sat down a second time anyway. The oath was never the problem, and the faith's own account is that the dissolution clause was.

name: The Gale Watch Oath
summary: Sworn by every Keeper on taking the rotation: to stand the hours, to open and close the pass on the flock's schedule and not on any other, and to refuse no traveller. It exists because a conscripted congregation cannot be asked for voluntary constancy, and because the only thing that makes a gate held by unpaid people defensible is that it cannot be shut on anybody.

attributes.what_is_sworn: To stand the rotation, to keep the crossing to the flock's dates, and to admit any traveller who asks, with no exception for rank, standing, price or pressure.
attributes.why_the_no_refusal_clause: Because a gate with a keeper who may refuse is a toll, and the Vigil's whole claim is that it holds a pass rather than a gate. This one clause is the reason the ridge is not what the Ninth Watch is.
attributes.how_it_is_sworn: Once per rotation, standing, with the pass behind the speaker. There is no rite and no text, because the whole oath is short enough to say over a mouthful of water.
attributes.what_it_forbids: Accepting money, carrying goods, sitting on the platform, and standing after the rotation ends. That last is the one actually broken and the one the ridge tolerates.
attributes.what_it_binds_without_belief: Nothing about belief. A Keeper need hold no doctrine at all, and the ridge has never once asked for more than the duty.
attributes.consequence: Because no Keeper may refuse entry, the toll is collected by the holder of the crossing and never by the faith, which is a legal separation both institutions depend on.
